  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.

  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
  """
  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  # Deliberately omits `scheduled_date`: a "created" entry's own
  # subject label (job → property/client) is enough to identify which
  # job this is, and surfacing it here would read as a schedule change
  # (`field_changes/1`'s "Scheduled date: ..." line) indistinguishable
  # from an actual reschedule recorded later by `update_job/3`.
  defp job_created_values(job) do
    %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a job's schedule and/or price — a reschedule, a price
  change, or both, made directly from the board rather than through
  `assign_cleaner/3`'s conflict-checked path. Records only the fields
  that actually changed to the audit trail, attributed to the caller.
  """
  def update_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset = Job.changeset(job, attrs)

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @audited_update_fields ~w(scheduled_date start_time end_time agreed_price_cents status)a

  defp record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated) do
    changed_fields =
      changeset.changes
      |> Map.keys()
      |> Enum.filter(&(&1 in @audited_update_fields))

    if changed_fields != [] do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        update_action(changed_fields),
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        audit_snapshot(job, changed_fields),
        audit_snapshot(updated, changed_fields)
      )
    end
  end

  defp update_action(changed_fields) do
    cond do
      Enum.any?(changed_fields, &(&1 in [:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])) ->
        "job_rescheduled"

      :agreed_price_cents in changed_fields ->
        "job_price_changed"

      true ->
        "job_updated"
    end
  end

  defp audit_snapshot(job, fields),
    do: Map.new(fields, &{to_string(&1), audit_value(Map.get(job, &1))})

  defp audit_value(%Date{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(%Time{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(value), do: value

  @doc """
  Removes a job from the board without hard-deleting its row — the
  row (and any audit entries already about it) stays resolvable for
  the trail. Distinct from `cancel_job/2`: this is the office
  correcting a mistaken entry rather than calling off an appointment,
  so it's recorded as "deleted" rather than "cancelled" and never
  notifies the assigned cleaner.
  """
  def delete_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_deleted",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs, actor: :system)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).

  ## Pay fields

  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
  itself.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :piece_rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while some spex drive the same form with a
  # `scheduled_date` override instead (matching the schema field name
  # directly). The form carries a second, always-blank
  # `job[scheduled_date]` field purely as a landing pad for that
  # override key (`Phoenix.LiveViewTest.form/3` requires an override's
  # key to match a real field name in the form). Whichever one arrives
  # non-blank wins; `scheduled_date` takes precedence when both do,
  # since a still-blank landing pad means only `date` was ever touched.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"scheduled_date" => sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, "date")

  defp rename_date_key(%{scheduled_date: sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, :date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients do
  @moduledoc """
  Clients and their properties: addresses, parking notes, entry
  methods and codes, pets, and cleaning preferences — the authoritative
  access and scope record every job carries.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.{Client, Property}
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder

  ## Clients

  def list_clients(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([c], asc: c.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_client!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Client{account_id: account_id}
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def change_client(%Scope{}, %Client{} = client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Client.changeset(client, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Lists only active clients, for the account's day-to-day client list.
  """
  def list_active_clients(%Scope{} = scope) do
    scope |> list_clients() |> Enum.filter(& &1.active)
  end

  def update_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    client
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  def deactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => false})
  end

  def reactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => true})
  end

  @doc """
  Permanently deletes a client and its properties.

  Refuses to delete a client that still has dependent records (e.g.
  scheduled jobs) elsewhere in the system — the database's foreign key
  constraints are the source of truth for what's "dependent," so this
  context stays ignorant of any other bounded context's schema.
  """
  def delete_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.delete(client)
  rescue
    Ecto.ConstraintError -> {:error, :has_upcoming_jobs}
  end

  ## Properties

  @doc """
  Lists a client's properties, ordered by address.
  """
  def list_properties(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{id: client_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id and p.client_id == ^client_id)
    |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_property!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_property(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Property{account_id: account_id}
    |> Property.changeset(attrs)
    |> validate_client_ownership(scope)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a property. When entry method, lockbox code, or alarm code
  change, records an audit entry naming the changed fields (never the
  code values themselves).
  """
  def update_property(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        %Property{} = property,
        attrs
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset =
      property
      |> Property.changeset(attrs)
      |> validate_client_ownership(scope)

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, updated.id)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def change_property(%Scope{}, %Property{} = property, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Property.changeset(property, attrs)
  end

  defp validate_client_ownership(changeset, %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) do
    case Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, :client_id) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      client_id ->
        query = where(Client, [c], c.id == ^client_id and c.account_id == ^account_id)

        if Repo.exists?(query) do
          changeset
        else
          Ecto.Changeset.add_error(changeset, :client_id, "is invalid")
        end
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists audit entries recorded against a property, most recent first.
  """
  def list_property_audit_entries(%Scope{} = scope, %Property{} = property) do
    Recorder.list_for_subject(scope, "Property", property.id)
  end

  defp record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, property_id) do
    changed_fields =
      Property.access_code_fields()
      |> Enum.filter(&Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, &1))
      |> Enum.map(&to_string/1)

    case changed_fields do
      [] ->
        :ok

      fields ->
        Recorder.record(scope, "access_details_updated", "Property", property_id, %{}, %{
          "changed_fields" => fields
        })
    end
  end
end

  ## Examples

      iex> change_user_password(user)
      %Ecto.Changeset{data: %User{}}

  """
  def change_user_password(user, attrs \\ %{}, opts \\ []) do
    User.password_changeset(user, attrs, opts)
  end

  @doc """
  Updates the user password.

  Returns a tuple with the updated user, as well as a list of expired tokens.

  ## Examples

      iex> update_user_password(user, %{password: ...})
      {:ok, {%User{}, [...]}}

      iex> update_user_password(user, %{password: "too short"})
      {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}}

  """
  def update_user_password(user, attrs) do
    user
    |> User.password_changeset(attrs)
    |> update_user_and_delete_all_tokens()
  end

  ## Session

  @doc """
  Generates a session token.
  """
  def generate_user_session_token(user) do
    {token, user_token} = UserToken.build_session_token(user)
    Repo.insert!(user_token)
    token
  end

  @doc """
  Gets the user with the given signed token.

  If the token is valid `{user, token_inserted_at}` is returned, otherwise `nil` is returned.
  """
  def get_user_by_session_token(token) do
    {:ok, query} = UserToken.verify_session_token_query(token)
    Repo.one(query)
  end

  @doc """
  Gets the user with the given magic link token.
  """
  def get_user_by_magic_link_token(token) do
    with {:ok, query} <- UserToken.verify_magic_link_token_query(token),
         {user, _token} <- Repo.one(query) do
      user
    else
      _ -> nil
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the user in by magic link.

  There are three cases to consider:

  1. The user has already confirmed their email. They are logged in
     and the magic link is expired.

  2. The user has not confirmed their email and no password is set.
     In this case, the user gets confirmed, logged in, and all tokens -
     including session ones - are expired. In theory, no other tokens
     exist but we delete all of them for best security practices.

  3. The user has not confirmed their email but a password is set.
     This cannot happen in the default implementation but may be the
     source of security pitfalls. See the "Mixing magic link and password registration" section of
     `mix help phx.gen.auth`.
  """
  def login_user_by_magic_link(token) do
    {:ok, query} = UserToken.verify_magic_link_token_query(token)

    case Repo.one(query) do
      # Prevent session fixation attacks by disallowing magic links for unconfirmed users with password
      {%User{confirmed_at: nil, hashed_password: hash}, _token} when not is_nil(hash) ->
        raise """
        magic link log in is not allowed for unconfirmed users with a password set!

        This cannot happen with the default implementation, which indicates that you
        might have adapted the code to a different use case. Please make sure to read the
        "Mixing magic link and password registration" section of `mix help phx.gen.auth`.
        """

      {%User{confirmed_at: nil} = user, _token} ->
        user
        |> User.confirm_changeset()
        |> update_user_and_delete_all_tokens()

      {user, token} ->
        Repo.delete!(token)
        {:ok, {user, []}}

      nil ->
        {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc ~S"""
  Delivers the update email instructions to the given user.

  ## Examples

      iex> deliver_user_update_email_instructions(user, current_email, &url(~p"/users/settings/confirm-email/#{&1}"))
      {:ok, %{to: ..., body: ...}}

  """
  def deliver_user_update_email_instructions(%User{} = user, current_email, update_email_url_fun)
      when is_function(update_email_url_fun, 1) do
    {encoded_token, user_token} = UserToken.build_email_token(user, "change:#{current_email}")

    Repo.insert!(user_token)
    UserNotifier.deliver_update_email_instructions(user, update_email_url_fun.(encoded_token))
  end

  @doc """
  Delivers the magic link login instructions to the given user.
  """
  def deliver_login_instructions(%User{} = user, magic_link_url_fun)
      when is_function(magic_link_url_fun, 1) do
    {encoded_token, user_token} = UserToken.build_email_token(user, "login")
    Repo.insert!(user_token)
    UserNotifier.deliver_login_instructions(user, magic_link_url_fun.(encoded_token))
  end

  @doc """
  Deletes the signed token with the given context.
  """
  def delete_user_session_token(token) do
    Repo.delete_all(from(UserToken, where: [token: ^token, context: "session"]))
    :ok
  end

  ## Token helper

  defp update_user_and_delete_all_tokens(changeset) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, user} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
        tokens_to_expire = Repo.all_by(UserToken, user_id: user.id)

        Repo.delete_all(from(t in UserToken, where: t.id in ^Enum.map(tokens_to_expire, & &1.id)))

        {:ok, {user, tokens_to_expire}}
      end
    end)
  end
end

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,

  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =

        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed

        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{

          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled,

  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, 2 * 3600, :second)

  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change

  #

  def user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs)

    token =
      extract_user_token(fn url ->
        Users.deliver_login_instructions(user, url)
      end)

    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)

  end

  def user_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    user_scope_fixture(user)
  end

  def user_scope_fixture(user) do
    Scope.for_user(user)
  end

  def set_password(user) do
    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: valid_user_password()})

    user
  end

  def extract_user_token(fun) do
    {:ok, captured_email} = fun.(&"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")

    # `fun` delivers through the real mailer (Swoosh's test adapter), so
    # this confirmation/login email it just sent is sitting in the
    # calling process's mailbox — an internal detail of building a
    # confirmed fixture user, not something the spec itself sent. Left
    # there, it's the *oldest* `{:email, _}` message, and
    # `assert_email_sent/1` always matches the oldest one first — so any
    # later, spec-relevant `assert_email_sent` would wrongly match this
    # one instead. Drain it now so it can't shadow that later assertion.
    receive do
      {:email, ^captured_email} -> :ok
    after
      0 -> :ok
    end

    [_, token | _] = String.split(captured_email.text_body, "[TOKEN]")

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.User do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  schema "users" do
    field :email, :string
    field :name, :string
    field :password, :string, virtual: true, redact: true
    field :hashed_password, :string, redact: true
    field :confirmed_at, :utc_datetime
    field :authenticated_at, :utc_datetime, virtual: true
    field :push_enabled, :boolean, default: true

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime)
  end

  @doc """
  A user changeset for registering or changing the email.

  It requires the email to change otherwise an error is added.

  Also casts `:push_enabled` — there's no dedicated settings changeset
  for it, and this is the only changeset `register_user/1` runs, so
  it's the one path that lets a cleaner fixture seed the preference.

  ## Options

    * `:validate_unique` - Set to false if you don't want to validate the
      uniqueness of the email, useful when displaying live validations.
      Defaults to `true`.
  """
  def email_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
    user
    |> cast(attrs, [:email, :push_enabled])
    |> validate_email(opts)
  end

  defp validate_email(changeset, opts) do
    changeset =
      changeset
      |> validate_required([:email])
      |> validate_format(:email, ~r/^[^@,;\s]+@[^@,;\s]+$/,
        message: "must have the @ sign and no spaces"
      )
      |> validate_length(:email, max: 160)

    if Keyword.get(opts, :validate_unique, true) do
      changeset
      |> unsafe_validate_unique(:email, CleanerCrm.Repo)
      |> unique_constraint(:email)
      |> validate_email_changed()
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  defp validate_email_changed(changeset) do
    if get_field(changeset, :email) && get_change(changeset, :email) == nil do
      add_error(changeset, :email, "did not change")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  @doc """
  A user changeset for changing the password.

  It is important to validate the length of the password, as long passwords may
  be very expensive to hash for certain algorithms.

  ## Options

    * `:hash_password` - Hashes the password so it can be stored securely
      in the database and ensures the password field is cleared to prevent
      leaks in the logs. If password hashing is not needed and clearing the
      password field is not desired (like when using this changeset for
      validations on a LiveView form), this option can be set to `false`.
      Defaults to `true`.
  """
  def password_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
    user
    |> cast(attrs, [:password])
    |> validate_confirmation(:password, message: "does not match password")
    |> validate_password(opts)
  end

  defp validate_password(changeset, opts) do
    changeset
    |> validate_required([:password])
    |> validate_length(:password, min: 12, max: 72)
    # Examples of additional password validation:
    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[a-z]/, message: "at least one lower case character")
    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[A-Z]/, message: "at least one upper case character")
    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[!?@#$%^&*_0-9]/, message: "at least one digit or punctuation character")
    |> maybe_hash_password(opts)
  end

  defp maybe_hash_password(changeset, opts) do
    hash_password? = Keyword.get(opts, :hash_password, true)
    password = get_change(changeset, :password)

    if hash_password? && password && changeset.valid? do
      changeset
      # If using Bcrypt, then further validate it is at most 72 bytes long
      |> validate_length(:password, max: 72, count: :bytes)
      # Hashing could be done with `Ecto.Changeset.prepare_changes/2`, but that
      # would keep the database transaction open longer and hurt performance.
      |> put_change(:hashed_password, Bcrypt.hash_pwd_salt(password))
      |> delete_change(:password)
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Confirms the account by setting `confirmed_at`.
  """
  def confirm_changeset(user) do
    now = DateTime.utc_now(:second)
    change(user, confirmed_at: now)
  end

  @doc """
  Verifies the password.

  If there is no user or the user doesn't have a password, we call
  `Bcrypt.no_user_verify/0` to avoid timing attacks.
  """
  def valid_password?(%CleanerCrm.Users.User{hashed_password: hashed_password}, password)
      when is_binary(hashed_password) and byte_size(password) > 0 do
    Bcrypt.verify_pass(password, hashed_password)
  end

  def valid_password?(_, _) do
    Bcrypt.no_user_verify()
    false
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, AccountsRepository, MembersRepository}
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{InvitationRepository, InvitationNotifier}
  alias CleanerCrm.Authorization
  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def subscribe_account(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account")
  end

  def subscribe_member(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member")
  end

  defp broadcast_account(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account", message)
  end

  defp broadcast_member(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member", message)
  end

  def list_accounts(%Scope{} = scope) do
    MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(scope.user.id)
  end

  def get_account(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    case AccountsRepository.get_account(id) do
      nil ->
        nil

      account ->
        case Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account.id) do
          false -> nil
          true -> account
        end
    end
  end

  def get_account!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    account = AccountsRepository.get_account!(id)
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account.id)
    account
  end

  def create_account(%Scope{} = scope, attrs) do
    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.create_account_with_owner(attrs, scope.user.id) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:created, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def update_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.update_account(account, attrs) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:updated, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def delete_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.delete_account(account) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:deleted, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def change_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)
    Account.changeset(account, attrs)
  end

  def list_account_members(%Scope{} = scope, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account_id)
    MembersRepository.list_account_members(account_id)
  end

  def add_user_to_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role \\ :member) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.add_user_to_account(user_id, account_id, role) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:created, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def remove_user_from_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_members, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.remove_user_from_account(user_id, account_id) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:deleted, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def update_user_role(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_members, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.update_user_role(user_id, account_id, role) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:updated, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def get_user_role(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account_id)
    MembersRepository.get_user_role(user_id, account_id)
  end

  def user_has_account_access?(%Scope{} = scope, account_id) do
    MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(scope.user.id, account_id)
  end

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Invitations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  def subscribe_invitations(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:invitations")
  end

  defp broadcast_invitation(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:invitations", message)
  end

  def invite_user(scope, account_id, email, role)
      when is_binary(email) and role in [:owner, :admin, :member] and not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id),
         :ok <- validate_user_not_already_member(email, account_id),
         {:ok, invitation} <- create_invitation(scope, account_id, email, role),
         :ok <- send_invitation_email(invitation) do
      broadcast_invitation(scope, {:created, invitation})
      {:ok, invitation}
    end
  end

  def accept_invitation(token, user_attrs) when is_binary(token) and is_map(user_attrs) do
    with {:ok, invitation} <- get_valid_invitation(token),
         {:ok, user} <- resolve_or_create_user(invitation, user_attrs),
         {:ok, member} <- accept_user_to_account(user, invitation),
         {:ok, _updated} <- InvitationRepository.accept(%Scope{}, invitation) do
      {:ok, {user, member}}
    end
  end

  def list_pending_invitations(scope, account_id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    if Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account_id) do
      InvitationRepository.list_pending_invitations(scope, account_id)
    else
      []
    end
  end

  def list_pending_invitations(_scope, nil), do: []

  def get_invitation_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    InvitationRepository.get_by_token_hash(token)
  end

  def cancel_invitation(scope, account_id, invitation_id)
      when is_integer(invitation_id) and not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id),
         invitation when not is_nil(invitation) <-
           InvitationRepository.get_invitation(scope, invitation_id),
         {:ok, cancelled} <- InvitationRepository.cancel(scope, invitation) do
      broadcast_invitation(scope, {:updated, cancelled})
      {:ok, cancelled}
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      error -> error
    end
  end

  def cleanup_expired_invitations do
    InvitationRepository.cleanup_expired_invitations(30)
    :ok
  end

  defp validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id) do
    if Authorization.authorize(:manage_members, scope, account_id),
      do: :ok,
      else: {:error, :not_authorized}
  end

  defp validate_user_not_already_member(email, account_id) do
    case Users.get_user_by_email(email) do
      nil ->
        :ok

      user ->
        if MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(user.id, account_id),
          do: {:error, :user_already_member},
          else: :ok
    end
  end

  defp create_invitation(scope, account_id, email, role) do
    attrs = %{
      email: email,
      role: role,
      account_id: account_id,
      invited_by_user_id: scope.user.id
    }

    InvitationRepository.create_invitation(scope, attrs)
  end

  defp send_invitation_email(invitation) do
    url = CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> "/invitations/accept/#{invitation.token}"

    case InvitationNotifier.deliver_invitation_email(invitation, url) do
      {:ok, _} -> :ok
      {:error, _} -> {:error, :email_delivery_failed}
    end
  end

  defp get_valid_invitation(token) do
    case InvitationRepository.get_by_token_hash(token) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :invalid_token}

      invitation ->
        cond do
          invitation.status != :pending ->
            {:error, :invalid_token}

          DateTime.compare(DateTime.utc_now(), invitation.expires_at) != :lt ->
            {:error, :expired_token}

          true ->
            {:ok, invitation}
        end
    end
  end

  defp resolve_or_create_user(invitation, %{email: provided_email} = user_attrs) do
    if provided_email == invitation.email do
      case Users.get_user_by_email(invitation.email) do
        nil -> Users.register_user(user_attrs)
        existing_user -> {:ok, existing_user}
      end
    else
      {:error, :email_mismatch}
    end
  end

  defp resolve_or_create_user(invitation, user_attrs) do
    user_attrs_with_email = Map.put(user_attrs, :email, invitation.email)

    case Users.get_user_by_email(invitation.email) do
      nil -> Users.register_user(user_attrs_with_email)
      existing_user -> {:ok, existing_user}
    end
  end

  defp accept_user_to_account(user, invitation) do
    inviter = Users.get_user!(invitation.invited_by_user_id)
    inviter_scope = %Scope{user: inviter, active_account_id: invitation.account_id}
    add_user_to_account(inviter_scope, user.id, invitation.account_id, invitation.role)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository do
  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, Member}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  def add_user_to_account(user_id, account_id, role \\ :member) do
    %Member{}
    |> Member.changeset(%{user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id, role: role})
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def remove_user_from_account(user_id, account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Member, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_found}

      member ->
        case member.role do
          :owner ->
            owner_count = count_owners(account_id)
            if owner_count > 1, do: Repo.delete(member), else: {:error, :last_owner}

          _ ->
            Repo.delete(member)
        end
    end
  end

  def update_user_role(user_id, account_id, role) do
    case Repo.get_by(Member, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_found}

      member ->
        changeset = Member.update_role_changeset(member, %{role: role})
        validated_changeset = Member.validate_owner_exists(changeset, Repo)

        case validated_changeset.valid? do
          true -> Repo.update(validated_changeset)
          false -> {:error, validated_changeset}
        end
    end
  end

  def get_user_role(user_id, account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Member, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> nil
      member -> member.role
    end
  end

  def user_has_account_access?(user_id, account_id) do
    Repo.exists?(from m in Member, where: m.user_id == ^user_id and m.account_id == ^account_id)
  end

  def can_add_user_to_account?(_account_id), do: true

  def count_account_users(account_id) do
    Repo.aggregate(from(m in Member, where: m.account_id == ^account_id), :count)
  end

  def list_user_accounts(user_id) do
    from(a in Account,
      join: m in Member,
      on: m.account_id == a.id,
      where: m.user_id == ^user_id
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def list_account_users(account_id) do
    from(u in User,
      join: m in Member,
      on: m.user_id == u.id,
      where: m.account_id == ^account_id
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def list_account_members(account_id) do
    from(m in Member,
      where: m.account_id == ^account_id,
      preload: [:user]
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def list_accounts_with_role(user_id, role) do
    from(a in Account,
      join: m in Member,
      on: m.account_id == a.id,
      where: m.user_id == ^user_id and m.role == ^role
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def by_user(user_id), do: from(m in Member, where: m.user_id == ^user_id)
  def by_account(account_id), do: from(m in Member, where: m.account_id == ^account_id)

    Repo.aggregate(
      from(m in Member, where: m.account_id == ^account_id and m.role == :owner),
      :count
    )
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t(),
          slug: String.t() | nil,
          drive_time_policy: :unpaid | :paid,
          members: [CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          users: [CleanerCrm.Users.User.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @reserved_slugs ~w(admin api www help support docs blog)

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "accounts" do
    field :name, :string
    field :slug, :string

    # Whether time spent driving between jobs counts toward a
    # cleaner's pay — read by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` alongside a
    # cleaner's earnings, set here rather than on a separate settings
    # table since it's the account's only pay policy so far.
    field :drive_time_policy, Ecto.Enum, values: [:unpaid, :paid], default: :unpaid

    has_many :members, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member, on_delete: :delete_all
    has_many :users, through: [:members, :user]

    timestamps()
  end

  def changeset(account, attrs) do
    account
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :slug, :drive_time_policy])
    |> validate_required([:name])
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 100)
    |> validate_slug()
    |> unique_constraint(:slug)
  end

  def create_changeset(attrs) do
    %__MODULE__{}
    |> changeset(attrs)
    |> maybe_generate_slug()
  end

  defp validate_slug(changeset) do
    changeset
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z0-9-]+$/,
      message: "must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens"
    )
    |> validate_length(:slug, min: 3, max: 50)
    |> validate_exclusion(:slug, @reserved_slugs, message: "is reserved and cannot be used")
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z]/, message: "must start with a letter")
  end

  defp maybe_generate_slug(changeset) do
    case get_field(changeset, :slug) do
      nil ->
        name = get_field(changeset, :name)
        if name, do: put_change(changeset, :slug, generate_slug(name)), else: changeset

      _ ->
        changeset
    end
  end

  defp generate_slug(name) do
    name
    |> String.downcase()
    |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]/, "-")
    |> String.replace(~r/-+/, "-")
    |> String.trim("-")
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset
  import Ecto.Query

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: integer(),
          role: :owner | :admin | :member,
          user_id: integer(),
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t(),
          user: CleanerCrm.Users.User.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          account: CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: NaiveDateTime.t(),
          updated_at: NaiveDateTime.t()
        }

  schema "members" do
    field :role, Ecto.Enum, values: [:owner, :admin, :member], default: :member

    belongs_to :user, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id

    timestamps()
  end

  def changeset(member, attrs) do
    member
    |> cast(attrs, [:role, :user_id, :account_id])
    |> validate_required([:role, :user_id, :account_id])
    |> validate_inclusion(:role, [:owner, :admin, :member])
    |> assoc_constraint(:user)
    |> assoc_constraint(:account)
    |> unique_constraint([:user_id, :account_id], name: :members_user_id_account_id_index)
  end

  def update_role_changeset(member, attrs) do
    member
    |> cast(attrs, [:role])
    |> validate_required([:role])
    |> validate_inclusion(:role, [:owner, :admin, :member])
  end

  def validate_owner_exists(changeset, repo) do
    case get_field(changeset, :role) do
      :owner ->
        changeset

      _ ->
        user_id = get_field(changeset, :user_id)
        account_id = get_field(changeset, :account_id)

        if user_id && account_id do
          case repo.get_by(__MODULE__, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
            %{role: :owner} ->
              owner_count =
                repo.aggregate(
                  from(m in __MODULE__, where: m.account_id == ^account_id and m.role == :owner),
                  :count
                )

              if owner_count <= 1 do
                add_error(changeset, :role, "account must have at least one owner")
              else
                changeset
              end

            _ ->
              changeset
          end
        else
          changeset
        end
    end
  end

  def has_role?(member, required_role) do
    role_hierarchy = %{member: 1, admin: 2, owner: 3}
    Map.get(role_hierarchy, member.role, 0) >= Map.get(role_hierarchy, required_role, 0)
  end

  def owner?(member), do: member.role == :owner
  def admin_or_owner?(member), do: member.role in [:admin, :owner]
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Authorization do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def authorize(action, %Scope{} = scope, resource) do
    case {action, resource} do
      {:read_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(scope.user.id, account_id)

      {:manage_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role in [:owner, :admin]

      {:manage_members, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role in [:owner, :admin]

      {:delete_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role == :owner

      _ ->
        false
    end
  end

  def authorize!(action, scope, resource) do
    unless authorize(action, scope, resource) do
      raise "Unauthorized: #{action} on #{inspect(resource)}"
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.AccountsRepository do
  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, Member}

  def create_account(attrs) do
    %Account{}
    |> Account.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def get_account(id), do: Repo.get(Account, id)
  def get_account!(id), do: Repo.get!(Account, id)

  def update_account(%Account{} = account, attrs) do
    account
    |> Account.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  def delete_account(%Account{} = account), do: Repo.delete(account)

  def create_account_with_owner(attrs, owner_id) do
    Repo.transaction(fn ->
      with {:ok, account} <- create_account(attrs),
           {:ok, _member} <-
             create_member(%{user_id: owner_id, account_id: account.id, role: :owner}) do
        account
      else
        {:error, reason} -> Repo.rollback(reason)
      end
    end)
  end

  def by_slug(slug), do: from(a in Account, where: a.slug == ^slug)
  def with_preloads(preloads), do: from(a in Account, preload: ^preloads)

  defp create_member(attrs) do
    %Member{}
    |> Member.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end
end

## Summary

Verified against the actual dev DB (read-only `SELECT`s only, no writes): the account `b4ecfdf7-95d9-4fc0-884a-353d9db1c473` ("QA Sparkle Cleaning Co"), the user `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` (id `1`, confirmed), and an `owner` membership row linking them all already exist. That matters because `register_cleaner/2` (below) requires `:manage_account` authorization, which checks for a real `owner`/`admin` membership row — confirmed present, so it'll succeed without any session/login flow.

### 1. Creating a cleaner — `CleanerCrm.Scheduling`

Two real (non-test) context functions are relevant:

```elixir
# lib/cleaner_crm/scheduling.ex:315-321
def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
    when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name)
```
Creates a placeholder-email `User` (no login capability) and adds them to the account as `:member` via `Accounts.add_user_to_account/4`. Returns `{:ok, %User{}}`. This is the production "Add cleaner" API used by the board.

```elixir
# lib/cleaner_crm/accounts.ex:86-93
def add_user_to_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role \\ :member)
```
Called internally by `register_cleaner/2`; requires `Authorization.authorize(:manage_account, scope, account_id)` — i.e. `scope.user` must have an `owner` or `admin` `Member` row on that account (`lib/cleaner_crm/authorization.ex:10-12`, checked via `MembersRepository.get_user_role/2`, `lib/cleaner_crm/accounts/members_repository.ex:47-52` — a live DB read, no session state involved).

There is no separate `Cleaner` schema — a cleaner is just a `CleanerCrm.Users.User` with a `CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member` row (`role: :member`) on the account. `belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User` on `Job` uses the default integer PK (`lib/cleaner_crm/scheduling/job.ex:73`, confirmed by `User`'s schema having no `@primary_key` override in `lib/cleaner_crm/users/user.ex`).

**Building a `Scope` for an existing user/account without a LiveView session** — mirror exactly what `lib/cleaner_crm_web/user_auth.ex:267-274` does at request time:

```elixir
# lib/cleaner_crm/users/scope.ex:21-32
defstruct user: nil, active_account: nil, active_account_id: nil
def for_user(%User{} = user), do: %__MODULE__{user: user}
```

```elixir
user = CleanerCrm.Users.get_user_by_email("qa-owner@cleanercrm.test")
account = CleanerCrm.Accounts.AccountsRepository.get_account!("b4ecfdf7-95d9-4fc0-884a-353d9db1c473")

scope = %{CleanerCrm.Users.Scope.for_user(user) | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
```

`for_user/1` alone leaves `active_account_id: nil`, which every context function pattern-matches against (`when not is_nil(account_id)`), so this manual merge step is required — it's the exact pattern `scope_with_active_account/1` uses in production.

### 2. Creating a client — `CleanerCrm.Clients`

```elixir
# lib/cleaner_crm/clients.ex:32-36
def create_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id)
```
Returns `{:ok, %Client{}} | {:error, changeset}`. Only `:name` is required (`Client.changeset`, `lib/cleaner_crm/clients/client.ex:41-46`, 1–200 chars). Castable fields: `:name, :active, :card_on_file, :email, :phone, :preferred_channel` (`:email`/`:sms`, default `:email`).

### 3. Creating a job — `CleanerCrm.Scheduling`

```elixir
# lib/cleaner_crm/scheduling.ex:45-54
def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
    when not is_nil(account_id)
```
`opts` accepts `actor: :system | :user` (default `:user`) — only affects audit-trail attribution, not required for QA data.

Castable fields (`Job.changeset`, `lib/cleaner_crm/scheduling/job.ex:79-89`): `client_id, property_id, cleaner_id, recurring_plan_id, scheduled_date, start_time, end_time, status, agreed_price_cents, agreed_price, pay_type, hourly_rate_cents, piece_rate_cents`.

`validate_required` (job.ex:86) only requires `:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time`. There's also a cross-field check: `end_time` must be strictly after `start_time` (job.ex:114-123, `validate_time_order`). `agreed_price` is a virtual `Decimal` in dollars that gets converted to `agreed_price_cents` for storage (job.ex:128-137) — pass either that or `agreed_price_cents` directly.

### 4. Does a job require `property_id`?

No. Per the schema moduledoc (job.ex:6-12): *"Both `client_id` and `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level... the schedule board's own job form always carries a property."* Neither is in `validate_required`. So a job can be created with only `client_id` and no property, but for QA data that faithfully mirrors what the real board writes, create a property per client first:

```elixir
# lib/cleaner_crm/clients.ex:98-104
def create_property(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id)
```
`Property.changeset` (`lib/cleaner_crm/clients/property.ex:60-69`) requires `:client_id` and `:service_address`, and `assoc_constraint(:client)`. `Clients.create_property/2` additionally runs `validate_client_ownership/2` (clients.ex:132-146), confirming the `client_id` belongs to the scope's `active_account_id`.
